findings.body: Every queued caller performs another manifest load after acquiring the lock instead of returning the already initialized cache, causing redundant serialized file I/O and increased cold-start request latency.
findings.failure_mode: Concurrent cache initialization becomes sequential and repeats the same work for each waiting request.
findings.impact: Every queued caller performs another manifest load after acquiring the lock instead of returning the already initialized cache, causing redundant serialized file I/O and increased cold-start request latency.
findings.root_cause: The new write-lock path does not repeat the cache check after the optimistic read.
findings.suggested_fix: After acquiring the write lock, recheck entryPointAssetsCache and return it for non-development environments before loading the manifest.
findings.title: Recheck the cache after acquiring the write lock
findings.trigger: Multiple non-development requests enter GetWebAssets while entryPointAssetsCache is nil; callers that observed nil queue for the write lock before the first loader publishes the result.
findings.verifier_reason: The patch adds Lock() at line 48 after the RLock/RUnlock check but does not recheck entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring the write lock. Multiple goroutines that observed nil under RLock will queue for the write lock and each will redundantly reload the manifest. The cited line exists verbatim, the cause is introduced by this patch, the trigger is realistic (concurrent cold-cache requests), and the impact (redundant I/O) follows logically.

raw_findings.body: The exclusive global lock remains held for the entire manifest read and processing operation, so concurrent development requests are serialized behind one another and can experience avoidable latency or timeout propagation.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A slow asset read blocks unrelated GetWebAssets callers for the duration of the I/O.
raw_findings.impact: The exclusive global lock remains held for the entire manifest read and processing operation, so concurrent development requests are serialized behind one another and can experience avoidable latency or timeout propagation.
raw_findings.root_cause: The mutex acquired for protecting the shared pointer also surrounds the potentially slow manifest-loading operation.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Load the manifest outside the mutex and lock only around the cache publication, using a second cache check or another single-flight mechanism for non-development initialization.
raw_findings.title: Do not hold the global write lock during manifest I/O in development mode
raw_findings.trigger: Concurrent requests run with cfg.Env == setting.Dev while reading assets-manifest.json is slow or temporarily blocked; development mode intentionally reloads assets on every request.

raw_findings.body: The intended race fix and cache-publication behavior are not protected by an automated regression test, so incomplete locking or future changes can pass the test suite and fail only under production concurrency.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Concurrency regressions in shared cache access remain undetected by the existing unit tests.
raw_findings.impact: The intended race fix and cache-publication behavior are not protected by an automated regression test, so incomplete locking or future changes can pass the test suite and fail only under production concurrency.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch changes global-cache synchronization without adding coverage for concurrent callers of the synchronized function.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a package-level test that resets the cache under the mutex, invokes GetWebAssets from multiple goroutines with a temporary manifest in both non-development and development modes, and runs it under the race detector.
raw_findings.title: Add a race-focused concurrent GetWebAssets test
raw_findings.trigger: Concurrent cold-cache and development-mode calls execute through the newly added read/write synchronization paths; the existing tests exercise only manifest parsing helpers and do not call GetWebAssets concurrently.

finding.title: Do not hold the global write lock during manifest I/O in development mode
finding.trigger: Concurrent requests run with cfg.Env == setting.Dev while reading assets-manifest.json is slow or temporarily blocked; development mode intentionally reloads assets on every request.
finding.verifier_reason: The claim targets development mode (cfg.Env == setting.Dev) where the cache is intentionally bypassed on every call (line 45 condition). Holding the lock during I/O in dev mode is by design to serialize reloads; it is not a defect introduced by this patch but expected behavior for hot-reload semantics. The impact is speculative and not a bug.
